name: Sidebar
summary: Side panel for apps: logo, search, main menu, secondary menu and the signed-in user. It can collapse to icons only. The two-level version has a rail with sections and a panel with the pages of one section.
use: Apps and portals with more than 5 sections.
Two-level: apps with many sections that each have their own pages.
avoid: Websites with few sections: use Header.
anatomy: Divider and user with sign-out button.
Two-level: rail (always icons only) and panel with title.
figmaProps: Dual adds the rail and the panel.
Icons only. Nav items switch to Collapsed=true.
reactProps: logoCollapsed shows when the sidebar is collapsed.
Usually a SearchInput (size sm) in <form role="search">.
Shows the collapse button when onCollapsedChange is set.
rail holds NavItems for sections. title is the panel heading.
behaviour: Fixed width 280px, collapsed 72px. Content scrolls when it does not fit.
Collapsed: labels are visually hidden and show as a tooltip on hover and focus. A count becomes a dot.
Focus stays on the collapse button after a toggle.
a11y: <aside> with two <nav> elements, each with its own label.
The collapse button has aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Collapsed items keep their name for screen readers, for example "Projects, 12 new".
Active page with aria-current="page" (via NavItem active).
content: Group sections in a logical order, most important at the top.
do: Collapse the sidebar on tablets and replace it with Bottom navigation on phones (below 600px). In Figma this follows responsive-components/sidebar/collapsed and sidebar/show.
Remember the collapsed state per user.
dont: More than about 9 items without grouping.
Collapse the sidebar without a way to expand it again.
open: Group headings are not there yet.
